You are being evaluated on Continual-ARC, a lifelong stream of ARC-style grid puzzles.
Each puzzle instance has a task id and a test input grid. Tasks recur across the
stream with fresh inputs. Each instance is a separate conversation: the next one
starts without this one's messages.

On every message you must choose exactly one action and put it as a JSON object
on the last line of your reply:
  {"action": "submit", "grid": [[0, 1, 2], [3, 4, 5]]}   submit an output grid
  {"action": "request_demos"}                            ask for one more demonstration pair for this task
  {"action": "finish"}                                   end the instance, once it is over
Grids are lists of rows; cells are integers 0-9; dimensions are 1-30.

Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown
with the input.

Scoring: an instance you solve costs 1 for each wrong submission and 1 for
each demo request. An instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt
cap is reached, and one that ends unsolved costs the whole budget, 16, however
many submissions and demo requests it used. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until
the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

# Continual-ARC task-4ab2d98c — solved (2026-10-20)

## Rule: translate the full picture down by one row

Keep the original grid dimensions. Move every cell down exactly one row; fill the new top row with the background color and clip/discard anything that would move past the bottom. Equivalently, for output row `r > 0`, copy input row `r-1`; output row 0 is all background. No horizontal movement, recoloring, or object filtering.

### Evidence
- Demo 1: background 1, foreground 8; the complete pictured form moves down one row (e.g. the isolated 8 in input row 9 appears at the same column in output row 10).
- Demo 2: background 2, foreground 9; output row 0 is all 2, output row 1 reproduces input row 0, and subsequent rows reproduce the preceding input row; the bottommost source row is clipped.
- Test: 29×23, background 8 and foreground 7. Applying the one-row downward translation was evaluator-confirmed correct.

### Reliable execution
Construct output by row-copying rather than manually redrawing cells: `[background_row] + input[:-1]`. This avoids transcription errors. In the solved run, several hand-written submissions implementing the right apparent rule were incorrect due to row/cell transcription; generating and verifying the exact shifted matrix fixed it. Demos suffice to infer the rule; no extra demos are needed for a recurrence of this pattern.
